standard_prerequisites.name: Delta_0 sentences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Delta_0 sentence is built from atomic formulas using propositional connectives and quantifiers that are all bounded by closed terms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The induction ranges over exactly this class of sentences, and each enumerated case matches one constructor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction on formula complexity
standard_prerequisites.statement: Each case may assume the counted statement for all immediate subformulas of the sentence under consideration.
standard_prerequisites.use: Every case except the base invokes the induction hypothesis on subformulas (2064-2133).

standard_prerequisites.name: Atomic completeness in Q
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a true closed atomic sentence, Q proves it; for a false one, Q proves its negation; the unit establishes this as its own lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the base case (2069-2070) and the atomic subcase of the final negation case (2124-2127).

standard_prerequisites.name: Bounded quantifiers versus finite instances
standard_prerequisites.statement: Q proves that a bounded universal quantifier over a closed-term bound is equivalent to the finite conjunction of its numeral instances, and dually for the bounded existential; the unit establishes this as its own lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the bounded-quantifier cases (2096-2117) into finite conjunctions and disjunctions already handled by the induction hypothesis.

core_obligations: Base case: a true atomic Delta_0 sentence is provable in Q by the unit's atomic completeness lemma (2069-2070).

Conjunction cases: for a true conjunction assemble the two provable conjuncts by logic; for a true negated conjunction one conjunct is false, prove its negation by the induction hypothesis and then the negated conjunction by logic (2073-2086).

Disjunction cases: for a true disjunction prove the true disjunct by the induction hypothesis and the disjunction by logic; for a true negated disjunction both disjuncts are false, so prove both negations and then the negated disjunction (2087-2095).

Bounded universal case: from the induction hypothesis on the numeral instances, derive the finite conjunction, and pass to the bounded quantifier through the unit's bounded-quantifier lemma; the negated case uses the Q-equivalence with a bounded existential (2096-2106).
Bounded existential case mirrors the bounded universal one, and its negation case uses the Q-equivalence with a bounded universal (2107-2117).

Final negation case: an atomic negated sentence goes through atomic completeness, and a double negation is stripped by logic in Q before invoking the induction hypothesis on the inner sentence (2118-2131).
Conclude that every true Delta_0 sentence is provable in Q (2064-2133).

proof_roadmap.step: Dispatch the base case by atomic completeness and set up the case split.
Discharge the four propositional cases by the induction hypothesis and logic.
Discharge the four bounded-quantifier cases through the bounded-quantifier equivalence in Q.
Discharge the remaining negation case by atomic completeness or double-negation elimination.

difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 2058-2062: if a Delta_0 sentence is true in the standard model then Q proves it. The author proof (2064-2133) is an induction on formula complexity whose induction step splits into nine explicitly enumerated cases: four propositional cases discharged by the induction hypothesis plus logic, four bounded-quantifier cases routed through the Q-provable equivalence between a bounded quantifier and a finite conjunction or disjunction of numerals instances, and a final negation case that falls back to atomic completeness or strips a double negation. Keeping the truth-in-the-standard-model side and the provability side aligned across all nine cases, and seeing which cited lemma each bounded-quantifier case needs, is a substantial bookkeeping argument rather than a routine verification.
